hook: A 1934 Art Deco school by Lewis P. Hobart and Bliss & Fairweather, its terra cotta panels carrying griffins.

historical_record.description: The Glen Park Grammar School was built on this parcel for the families who settled Glen Park after 1906 — a three-story Mission Revival building with shaped parapets and a detached auditorium reached by a one-story passage. It taught first through eighth grade and was replaced in 1934.

A new Glen Park Elementary School was built here with Public Works Administration funding, replacing the wood-frame school put up after the 1906 earthquake. Bliss & Fairweather and Lewis Hobart designed it in the PWA Moderne style in fireproof concrete, in three phases: the 18-classroom academic building on Lippard Street in 1935, the kindergarten wing on Brompton Street in 1938 and the auditorium on Bosworth Street in 1939. It opened to neighbourhood children on 9 November 1937.
Glen Park School, designed by John Bakewell Jr.
Chain link fences were added to the concrete retaining walls, five years after the school was completed.
A concrete pedestrian ramp was built over Bosworth Street, after the city widened it to four lanes in 1964; small sections of the retaining wall at the northern boundary were removed for it.
Accessibility upgrades added entrances, drinking fountains, bathrooms and handrails, the largest exterior change being a new ramp and entrance on the east elevation at the northern playground.
Recommended for city landmark designation in 2023, on historical, aesthetic and artistic grounds.

historic_survey.finding: Appears eligible for the National Register and the California Register under Criteria A/1 and C/3, and as a San Francisco City Landmark
historic_survey.physical_integrity: High; retains location, setting, design, workmanship, materials, feeling and association
historic_survey.note: One of eight parcels the evaluation surveyed intensively. It was funded by a 1933 Public Works Administration loan and grant, alongside George Washington High School, Marina Junior High School, Lawton Elementary School and Visitacion Valley School, and built in three phases under PWA project numbers 7942.04, 7942.12 and 1578.0. Its terra cotta detailing follows Bliss & Fairweather's post office at Stockton. The original wood-sash multi-light awning and hopper windows have been replaced with metal sash in the same openings, on a date the school district's drawings do not record.

building.completed_conflict: The city's New Deal survey dates the school's first phase, the academic building on Lippard Street, to 1935; the assessor's roll gives 1934.

unknowns: The city's New Deal survey gives the school as 151 Lippard Street in its project table and as 151 Lippard Avenue in its landmark recommendations; the city's address registry has only Lippard Avenue.
